briefing.text: The cohort may be a TRK-fusion-selected series (clinical columns such as POS_ARCHER, POS_IMPACT, ANY_LINE_NTRK point that way), so there may be few or no fusion-negative samples to compare against. Count samples with and without a confirmed NTRK1/2/3 fusion, using data_sv.txt and the POS_* columns. The study is about TRK fusions and holds a TMB variable, so under the benchmark convention a missing internal comparator does not make the hypothesis Not verifiable. If no negatives exist, decide True/False by comparing the cohort's TMB with known pan-cancer fusion-negative TMB levels and established biology on kinase-fusion-driven tumours, and say which kind of evidence decided the label.
briefing.reason: Stops a wrong 'Not verifiable' when there is no internal comparator, and names the fallback evidence.

briefing.text: TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS cannot be compared across assays. Samples with the -AS suffix (Archer RNA fusion panel) have no DNA mutation calls. MSK-IMPACT versions (IM3/IM5/IM6/IM7) cover different numbers of megabases, and the panel matrix may wrongly label everything WXS. Group TMB by sample-ID suffix and panel. Treat TMB for Archer-only samples as missing, not zero, and use per-Mb (panel-normalised) values instead of raw mutation counts.
briefing.reason: Counting RNA-only samples as zero TMB, or using raw counts across panels, would bias any comparison.

briefing.text: Some patients have more than one sample (e.g. T01 and T02). Count SAMPLE_ID per PATIENT_ID and keep one DNA (IMPACT) sample per patient before comparing groups.

Not every NTRK structural variant is a functional TRK fusion. Out-of-frame events, events that lose the 3' kinase domain, and intragenic rearrangements (e.g. an NTRK2-STRN deletion with unknown frame) may not be oncogenic, and data_sv.txt may disagree with the clinical POS_* fields. Define fusion status mainly from the study's clinical confirmation columns, and run a sensitivity analysis using SV-derived status.
briefing.reason: How fusion-positive is defined decides who sits in each group.

briefing.text: TMB is very right-skewed. A few MSI-high or hypermutated tumours can dominate means and push a group's average up; colorectal NTRK-fusion cancers are notably enriched for MSI-H/MLH1 silencing. Flag samples with TMB>20 mut/Mb and colorectal/MSI cases. Use medians and Mann-Whitney or log-TMB, and report results with and without these outliers.
briefing.reason: Outliers can flip the direction of a mean-based comparison.

briefing.text: Cancer type confounds TMB: melanoma and lung are high, while sarcoma, thyroid, salivary and paediatric tumours are low. TRK fusions are enriched in rare, typically low-TMB histologies such as secretory carcinoma, infantile fibrosarcoma and papillary thyroid carcinoma. Cross-tabulate fusion status by CANCER_TYPE and age, and compare within cancer type (stratified test, or regression of log TMB with a cancer-type term) as well as pooled.
briefing.reason: A pooled comparison can reflect histology mix rather than fusion status.

shared_assumptions: Both teams read TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS as mutations per megabase on the usual clinical scale. The values are all multiples of 1/30 (0.0333, 0.0667, ...), which suggests a mutation count divided by 30 Mb (an exome-sized denominator) applied to targeted-panel samples. If so, the deposited values understate per-Mb TMB by roughly 25-30x, and the 'very low TMB' description (median ~0, max 2.3) may be a scaling artifact.

Both teams assumed that, with no fusion-negative group in the tables, the comparison must be made against an external pan-cancer reference. They also assumed that comparing a deposited score on an unknown scale with literature mut/Mb values is valid.
Both treated the cohort as one group. The hypothesis may hold or fail by histology, for example colorectal fusion-positive tumours versus the rest.
unused_evidence: data_mutations.txt: neither team recounted nonsynonymous mutations per sample to check what TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS was computed from, or to rebuild per-Mb TMB with the correct panel size. The IM3/IM5/IM6 suffixes in the sample IDs mark different panel versions, each with its own footprint.
data_gene_panel_matrix.txt labels every sample 'WXS' even though the IDs are IMPACT panel samples. This conflicts with the sample IDs and bears directly on the denominator.
Neither team derived MSI or hypermutator status, for example by checking MLH1/MSH2/MSH6/PMS2/POLE alterations in the mutation and CNA files for the highest-TMB colorectal samples.
The timeline and patient tables (immunotherapy lines, best response) were not used. They are probably irrelevant to TMB direction.
unresolved_weak_points: Both teams named the unclear TMB scale as a weak point, and neither resolved it. Their 'False' rests partly on how low the absolute values look.

Both teams named the missing fusion-negative comparator. They reported it but answered it only with a qualitative appeal to biology. Neither stated which reference TMB values were used or on what scale.
second_readings: Reading 1: fusion-positive cancers as a whole have higher TMB than fusion-negative cancers. Reading 2: within a histology (e.g. colorectal), fusion-positive tumours have higher TMB. Colorectal TRK-fusion tumours are often MSI-high, so the two readings could point in different directions.
'Higher' could mean the median or the mean. A few hypermutated samples could make the mean high while the median stays low.
challenge.verdict: Moderate trust in 'False'. Fusion-positive tumours with a quiet genome background is plausible biology, and the label probably holds. But both teams leaned on absolute TMB values that look mis-scaled (count/30 Mb on panel data), and neither addressed a possible MSI-high colorectal subgroup. The reasoning needs these checks before release.

If so, and you recompute TMB per Mb with the panel footprint (IM3/IM5/IM6), are melanoma and NSCLC still 'near 0', and does your comparison with typical histology TMB change?

How is TMB (nonsynonymous) computed and normalised in public cancer-genomics portal study files for targeted-panel samples? Specifically, is a fixed 30 Mb denominator ever applied regardless of panel size?
questions.why: The deposited values are exact multiples of 1/30. Whether the score is per-Mb or count/30 decides whether the cohort's TMB is truly low.

questions.question: In published pan-cancer analyses of NTRK fusion-positive tumours, how does TMB compare with fusion-negative tumours, overall and within colorectal cancer, and how common is MSI-high in NTRK fusion-positive colorectal cancer?
questions.why: There is no internal comparator, so the label depends on established biology, and the colorectal/MSI subgroup could reverse the direction under a within-histology reading.

findings.question: How is TMB (nonsynonymous) computed and normalised in public cancer-genomics portal study files for targeted-panel samples? Is a fixed 30 Mb denominator ever applied regardless of panel size?
findings.answer: UNVERIFIED (web research tool returned HTTP 403 on every call; answer from domain knowledge). cBioPortal TMB (nonsynonymous) = nonsynonymous somatic mutation count / profiled size in Mb from the sample's gene panel. If a sample is labelled WES/WXS or has no panel size, a default ~30 Mb exome denominator is used. Values that are exact multiples of 1/30 therefore indicate count/30, regardless of the real panel size (~0.9-1.2 Mb for MSK-IMPACT). This keeps ranks within a panel but understates true mut/Mb by ~25-30x. So 'low' absolute values partly reflect the denominator, and comparisons should use ranks or counts.

findings.question: In published pan-cancer analyses of NTRK fusion-positive tumours, how does TMB compare with fusion-negative tumours, overall and within colorectal cancer, and how common is MSI-high in NTRK fusion-positive colorectal cancer?
findings.answer: UNVERIFIED (research tool down; recalled literature, not read). Pan-cancer (e.g. Rosen et al., Clin Cancer Res 2020, MSK-IMPACT): TRK fusion-positive tumours generally have lower TMB than fusion-negative tumours and lack canonical drivers, which contradicts the hypothesis. Colorectal cancer is the exception: NTRK fusion-positive CRCs are strongly enriched for MSI-high/MLH1 promoter hypermethylation (in most series, most of these cases are MSI-H; cf. Cocco et al. Ann Oncol 2019; Pietrantonio et al. JNCI 2017). Within CRC, their TMB is therefore higher than in fusion-negative CRC. The established pan-cancer direction supports 'False'.
